newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat up, then falters, on EU export news.
newsitem.headline: French wheat up, then falters, on EU export news.

text.p: French wheat prices rose in late trading on Thursday after the European Union more than doubled its wheat exports at this week's export tender from the previous week's sale, grain traders said.

But after picking up about five francs a tonne on the sale of more than 400,000 tonnes of EU wheat, prices showed signs of trailing off, with world markets bringing new proof that EU wheat is sharply undercut by Argentina, they said.
Rouen-delivered wheat gained five francs to 850 francs for January (or 840 for January-March, 835 for February-April), excluding carrying charges, traders said.
These mid-range prices then quickly became sellers' offering prices, traders said.
Tunisia bought wheat on the world market at a level estimated by on etrader at around $135 per tonne in EU terms.
That compared with $148-149 per tonne for subsidised wheat exports in the latest EU tender, showing the EU is still well above the Argentine market, traders said.
Argentina is expcted to supply part or all of Tunisia's 100,000-tonne purchase.
